messages:
alex_support: Hey team — customer hitting repeated failures when the model tries to call our file_ops function. API responds with 'malformed tool args'. Repro + request id below (req_0a1b2c3d).

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{
    \"model\": \"redwood-1\",
    \"messages\": [{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"list files\"}],
    \"functions\": [{\"name\":\"file_ops\",\"arguments\": {\"path\": \"C:\\Users\\alice\\data\\\", \"options\": {\"recursive\": true,},},}]
  }'
```

Response:
```json
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{\"error\":\"malformed tool args: Unexpected token '}' in JSON at position 134\"}
```

Customer says this started after upgrading SDK to 0.12.4. Low traffic but high impact. Any quick checks?

samir_eng: Can you paste the raw request body we receive (from logs) for req_0a1b2c3d? Suspect either trailing commas or an extra escaping pass from the SDK. Also which SDK (node/python) and exact version?

alex_support: Got the server-side capture attached below (sanitized). This is the raw body our gateway forwarded:

```
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-1\",
  \"messages\": [{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"list files\"}],
  \"functions\": [{\"name\":\"file_ops\",\"arguments\": {\"path\": \"C:\\Users\\alice\\data\\\", \"options\": {\"recursive\": true,},},}]
}
```
So two problems visible: trailing commas inside the nested objects and the Windows path with backslashes. The SDK supposedly constructs the arguments object; maybe it serializes twice.

devx: Thanks — that raw capture is super helpful. Two points: (1) Strict JSON parsers choke on trailing commas, so those will cause a parse failure. (2) Backslashes are only a problem if they're not escaped when embedding JSON inside a string. If the SDK stringifies arguments and then our service tries to parse them again, the backslashes might have been consumed or left unescaped. Can you confirm if functions.arguments is being sent as an object or a JSON-encoded string?

alex_support: According to the SDK code path the user took (node sdk v0.12.4), functions.arguments is passed as a JS object, but we have a known regression where the Node client \"helpfully\" JSON.stringify's the arguments field before sending; newer runtime code expects the HTTP body to contain raw objects. This double-serialization would produce embedded quotes and require backslashes to be escaped twice.

samir_eng: That matches my hunch. Quick repro I tried locally: if I send the body with trailing commas I get the same error. If I remove trailing commas and properly escape path backslashes the call proceeds to the function. Example working arguments snippet:

```
\"functions\": [{
  \"name\": \"file_ops\",
  \"arguments\": {\"path\": \"C:\\Users\\alice\\data\\\", \"options\": {\"recursive\": true}}
}]
```

Note: no trailing commas and path backslashes are escaped (\\).

devx: Short term: advise customer to remove trailing commas and ensure paths are double-escaped in Node strings (e.g., use `C:\\\\Users\\\\alice\\\\data\\\\` if the SDK stringifies twice). Longer term: we'll patch the Node SDK to stop double-stringifying and add stricter validation and a clearer error message (INC-4821).

infra-bot: INC-4821 created: \"node sdk 0.12.4 double-serializes function args -> causes malformed tool args on server\". Priority: P2. Assignee: samir_eng.

jane_prod: Is there a mitigation we can push server-side? If we attempt to detect and auto-parse a JSON string in functions.arguments, we risk silently changing behavior. I'd prefer we improve the error text to say: \"expected JSON object for functions.arguments but received invalid JSON (trailing comma or unescaped backslashes). Check SDK versions.\"

ops_eli: I've added a small validation layer to return a friendly error that surfaces both: (a) \"trailing comma\" and (b) \"unescaped backslashes\" when detected heuristically. Patch will go to staging later today.

alex_support: Customer applied workaround (removed trailing comma and escaped path) and reports success in QA. They were able to proceed to production after applying the fix.

devx: Follow-ups: (1) Node SDK patch to be released v0.12.5 with fix and tests. (2) Docs update: examples for function args with Windows paths + note about no trailing commas. (3) Improve server error messages per Jane.

alex_support: Thanks everyone — closing on our side once INC-4821 is resolved and docs updated :thumbsup:
